items.synopsis: A system with LC1301 and SF5 raises a fabric capacity alarm rather than major link fault alarms when minor fabric degradation occurs.
items.description: LC1301 with SF5 platforms: isolated fabric link faults could trigger major alarms despite minimal impact to overall fabric operation. The system now raises a "less than acceptable fabric capacity" alarm when fabric capacity falls below platform-defined thresholds.

items.category: Tracking interface specific issues for Aegon Line card
items.synopsis: Interfaces remain down on PTX10008/PTX10004 with LC1301 line cards when 2X100G speed is configured before QSFP optics insertion
items.description: On PTX10008 and PTX10004 platforms running Junos Evolved affected releases with LC1301 line cards, Ethernet interfaces remain down when the 2x100G interface speed is configured before Quad Small Formfactor Pluggable (QSFP) transceivers are inserted and the optical signal is up. This condition affects dataplane connectivity and can result in loss of traffic on the impacted interfaces.

items.synopsis: Junos EVO platform fails to recognize a SIB card after it experiences a power failure
items.description: On PTX10004, PTX10008 and PTX10016 platforms running Junos OS Evolved, when a Switch Interface Board (SIB) experiences a power failure and is later replaced with a healthy SIB, the device fails to recognize the installed SIB. The affected SIB slot remains in an Empty state, resulting in reduced switch fabric capacity, loss of fabric redundancy, and potential traffic impact under load.

items.synopsis: The interface fails to come up after FPC reboot if the streaming server and export profile are not configured correctly
items.description: On all Junos and Junos evolved platforms with telemetry enabled, if the streaming server and export profile for reporting-rate are not properly configured in the analytics settings, rebooting the FPC would prevent any of the interfaces from coming up.

items.synopsis: Junos Evolved platfrom, when gNMI collecting data from "optics/lanediags/lane/lane_laser_receiver_power_dbm" and "optics/lanediags/lane/lane_laser_output_power_dbm" are unreadable
items.description: The JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) encoding of leafs of type "ieeefloat32"([https://github.com/openconfig/public/blob/master/release/models/types/openconfig-types.yang#L127)](https://github.com/openconfig/public/blob/master/release/models/types/openconfig-types.yang#L127)) is not correct, causing gRPC Network Management Interface (gNMI) data outputs unreadable.

items.synopsis: The sysd process crashes with error logs upon exceeding its memory limit
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved platforms with telemetry streaming configured, the sysd (System Daemon) process crashes on the backup RE (Routing Engine), and error logs are observed when sysd memory usage continues to grow over time, and the memory limit is exceeded. This issue is observed when the 64-bit sysd consumes more memory than the configured system limit when the device has been running for a long time (typically more than 100 days) in the dual RE scenario.

items.synopsis: NA-GRPCD process crashes when the collector terminates where the dial-out telemetry sensor is added through CLI configuration
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved platforms, the na-grpcd process crashes where dail-out telemetry is enabled and sensor is added through CLI configuration and the collector is terminated. This does not impact any service.

items.synopsis: Interfaces take 30 seconds to come up for a short LOS event
items.description: On PTX10002-36QDD, interfaces take 30 seconds to come up for a short LOS (Loss of Signal) event.

items.synopsis: BGP Prefix-SID Label collision causing RPD crash
items.description: On all Junos and Junos OS Evolved platforms, In Segment Routing the RPD ( Routing Protocol Daemon ) crash was observed due to different prefixes were trying to use same label, when Bgp prefix SID ( Segment Identifier ) feature was configured and labels were derived using the SID index.

items.synopsis: BGP session teardown due to incorrect 'prefix-limit maximum exceeded' error when RIB sharding is enabled
items.description: On all Junos and Junos OS Evolved platforms, when prefix-limit or accepted-prefix-limit is configured under family route-target with rib-sharding, prefix-limit will be incorrectly reported as 'prefix-limit maximum is exceeded'. This causes the BGP session to go down immediately. This occurs because the system incorrectly counts each received route multiple times (once for the main thread and once for each shard)

items.synopsis: BMP traces continues to fill the trace file even after removing BMP traceoptions configuration
items.description: On all Junos OS and Junos OS Evolved platforms, enabling BMP(BGP Monitoring Protocol) tracing with local-rib monitoring continues to fill the trace file even after removing BMP trace option Configuration it is still running this on a cRPD instance, this creates a risk of the space exhaustion on a host that contains other production cRPDs.

items.category: Track PRs in BGP Flow Spec area & is part of BGP inside RPD.
items.synopsis: BGP IPv6 Flow Specification Session Flapping When inet6-flow Is Enabled
items.description: In certain Junos OS releases, BGP sessions may repeatedly reset when IPv6 Flow Specification (inet6-flow) is enabled. This behavior occurs when the router receives specific IPv6 Flow Specification updates that include a default (wildcard) match. Earlier releases do not exhibit this behavior, leading to a difference in observed stability when upgrading.

items.synopsis: PICD process core observed on device
items.description: On all Junos OS Evolved platforms, due to software segmentation fault, optics firmware reports a max_lane_count greater than 8. This causes the picd process to core resulting in traffic loss. This is a rare issue.

items.category: QOS issues in EVO for BCM XGS Platforms
items.synopsis: Intermittent evo-pfemand crash when SNMP query is performed immediately after PFE restart
items.description: On all Junos Evolved platforms, the evo-pfemand crashes intermittently when interface statistics is fetched through SNMP (Simple Network Management Protocol) query immediately after PFE (Packet Forwarding Engine) restart. This issue is seen after multiple PFE restarts and recovers after the evo-pfemand restart.

items.category: PFE COS features on BT based platforms
items.synopsis: 10G channelized interface fails to reach full line rate due to low-rate queue overscheduling
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved PTX10004, PTX10008 and PTX10016 platforms using LC1201 or LC1202 line cards, a 10G channelized interface created from a 100G or 400G port may fail to reach full line rate. This issue occurs because the interface cannot fully utilize the link due to scheduler behavior when the interface has more than 4 channels and one or more output queues are set to a 5% or lower rate limit and receive a very high offered load compared to other queues.

items.category: PFE L2 forwarding features on BT based platforms
items.synopsis: On PTX EVO platforms in EVPN-VXLAN scenario traffic will not egress out of the irb next-hop when the bridge-domain doesn't have VXLAN VNI configured
items.description: On all PTX Evolved platforms that support EVPN-VXLAN (Ethernet VPN-Virtual Extensible LAN), when the PTX router acts as a MAC-VRF (Media Access Control - Virtual Routing and Forwarding) EVPN gateway, it will fail to forward traffic routed through the 'irb' interface due to packets being discarded at PFE (packet forwarding Engine), causing packet loss.

items.synopsis: ASIC error triggers PFE disable state on PTX10002-36QDD platform and LC1301 line card with active counter processing
items.description: On PTX10002-36QDD platform and LC1301 line card, under high-traffic conditions with active counter processing on a loopback interface, an ASIC error may be triggered, causing the Packet Forwarding Engine (PFE) to enter a disabled state. This results in all interfaces going down and leads to complete traffic loss.

items.synopsis: Traffic drops in 6VPE deployments without IPv6 enabled core interfaces
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved PTX platforms, the traffic will be dropped when IPv6 traffic is over IPv4 MPLS (Multiprotocol Label Switching.) tunnel under BGP (Border Gateway Protocol) 6VPE (IPv6 VPN Provider Edge) environment.

items.synopsis: Correct values of ACCTG-Terminate-cause are not getting populated in ACCTG-STOP message.
items.description: Correct values of ACCTG-Terminate-cause are not getting populated in ACCTG-STOP message for few scenarios as mentioned below: Ageout of client mac clear ethernet-switching-table clear dot1x interface

items.synopsis: Traffic dropped after priority change in VRRP with EVPN-VxLAN scenario
items.description: On all Junos and Junos Evolved platforms, in Virtual Router Redundancy Protocol (VRRP) with Ethernet Virtual Private Network - Virtual Extensible Local Area Network (EVPN-VXLAN) scenario, when VRRP priority is changed, the VRRP virtual Media Access Control (MAC) address can remain pinned as a static entry on the remote device. As a result, MAC movement does not occur correctly, and VRRP packets are dropped on the leaf device. This impacts VRRP operation after priority changes.

items.synopsis: Commit error when deleting interface with hierarchical scheduler enabled
items.description: On ACX7100 and ACX7348 platforms running Junos EVO 24.4R1, a commit error may occur when attempting to delete an interface (IFD) that has the hierarchical scheduler enabled and configured. The hierarchical scheduler is a required dependency for the output traffic control profile applied on interface sets (IFLSET). During commit validation, this dependency is enforced, preventing interface deletion until associated hierarchical scheduler configurations are deactivated.

items.category: Host path software for ACX platform
items.synopsis: DHCP clients do not come up when VRF leak and "dhcp-relay" with "no-snoop" are configured under a routing-instance
items.description: On all Junos OS Evolved ACX7K Series platforms, when DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) relay mode is used within a routing-instance scenario, DHCP clients fail to come up because DHCP offer packets are being dropped.

items.category: Host path software for ACX platform
items.synopsis: Error messages are seen on Junos OS Evolved ACX and QFX platforms
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved ACX and QFX platforms, when "set system ddos-protection protocol " is configured or ddos-protection configuration is deleted or when "show ddos-protection protocol" is executed then below logs will be seen.DDOS:POLICE: DdosPolicer does not exist DDOS:POLICE: Ddos group does not exist.

items.synopsis: L3VPN traffic drop due to incorrect destination MAC after MAC move in core
items.description: On all Junos OS Evolved ACK7K platforms, When a Media Access Control (MAC) address change or move occurs on the core side of the ingress Provider Edge (PE) node in a Layer 3 Virtual Private Network (L3VPN) topology, the ingress PE correctly updates the unicast Internet Protocol version 4 (IPv4) next-hop via Address Resolution Protocol (ARP); however, the dependent IPv4 to Multiprotocol Label Switching (MPLS) (indirect) L3VPN next-hop fails to update its destination MAC address. As a result, L3VPN MPLS traffic is forwarded with a stale destination MAC address, leading to incorrect packet forwarding and service impact.

items.synopsis: VPLS Layer 2 multicast traffic might be duplicated after output traffic control profile or HCOS interface configuration changes
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved ACX platforms, when HCOS (Hierarchical Class of Service) and class of service are enabled for VPLS (Virtual Private LAN Service), deactivating and reactivating the output-traffic-control-profile or making HCOS interface configuration changes might cause L2 (Layer 2) multicast traffic to be duplicated toward the access interface.

items.synopsis: High memory usage is showing, when we configure unsupported licensing feature
items.description: On all Junos EX and QFX platforms operating in an EVPN (Ethernet Virtual Private Network) environment, this issue occurs when the CLI command 'licensing hourly update' is executed on a device that does not support the licensing feature.

items.synopsis: PyEZ Issue, failing on RPC request "show arp interface <>" to EVO platforms
items.description: On all Junos Evolved platforms, on invalid interface fetching, display error is seen on "show arp interface <>" command.

items.synopsis: Prolonged commit time with largescale lo0 filter binds cause configuration load failure
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved platforms, commit operations with ~38005000 lo0 filter binds take ~4m42s (vs <1m expected). If commit exceeds 5 minutes, mgd times out, which cause configuration load failure and service impact.

items.category: Issues related to debug utilties - objmon, objshell/Dashboard
items.synopsis: [EVO] snmp get-next on hrStorage mib fails every 10 seconds

items.category: EVO Netstack Juniper Tunnel Driver Module
items.synopsis: The LDP session does not come up when an IPsec SA is configured under OSPFv3
items.description: On Junos Evolved platforms, when Open Shortest Path First version 3 (OSPFv3) Internet Protocol Security (IPsec) SA is applied at the interface (IFD/IFL) level, Label Distribution Protocol (LDP) is able to discover the neighbor via User Datagram Protocol (UDP) Hellos, but fails to bring up the Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) session, preventing the LDP session from becoming operational. Disabling the OSPFv3 IPsec SA immediately restores normal LDP operation. During the service impact, the session will be down and traffic will not be send. Once the LDP session comes up, traffic can be routed through it.

items.synopsis: RTC time sync delay after reboot on Junos OS Evolved platforms
items.description: On all Junos OS Evolved platforms, due to linux kernel issue, periodical sync from system time to RTC (Real-Time Communication) every 11min stops working when system time moves to backwards.

items.category: Express PFE Tunnels on ptx-evo platforms
items.synopsis: UDP Source Port cannot hash when using FTI tunnel interface for MPLS traffic
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved PTX Series platforms with incoming MPLS packets and outgoing MPLS over UDP configured over a Flexible Tunnel Interface (FTI), MPLS over UDP traffic for the same label would have the same source port. This would affect load balancing mechanism and can lead to inefficient utilization of links.

items.synopsis: BGP/LDP sessions flap due to TCP sequence number wraparound when TCP-AO is enabled
items.description: On all Junos OS Evolved platforms, Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) or Label Distribution Protocol (LDP) sessions will intermittently flap when Transmission Control Protocol-Authentication Option (TCP-AO) is enabled under high traffic or long-lived connections due to TCP sequence number rollover, leading to TCP authentication failures. The issue is primarily observed in interoperability scenarios and does not cause system crashes.

items.synopsis: Certain Junos EVO applications may become unresponsive during trace file rotation
items.description: On Junos EVO platforms, frequent trace file rotation may cause certain EVO applications to become unresponsive.

items.synopsis: CLI session timeout clears terminal scroll back
items.description: On all Junos OS Evolved platforms, when a CLI(Command Line Interface) session times out, it triggers a terminal reset which clears the visible screen and scrollback buffer. As a result, users are unable to view previous command outputs.

items.synopsis: SNMP traps related to optics/optic's media lane alarms will not be raised
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved platforms, SNMP(Simple Network Management Protocol) management systems do not receive related to optics or transceiver lane and module alarm traps.

items.synopsis: IM NH table synchronization failures during Routing Engine switchover
items.description: On all Junos and Junos Evolved platforms configured with Multiple Protocol Label Switch (MPLS) Virtual Private Network (VPN) services profiles, repeated backtoback routing engine (RE) switchovers can cause an RE0toRE1 switchover to fail to populate Internal Memory Next-Hop (IM NH) table entries, resulting in lookup related errors and impacting the forwarding of Broadcast, Unknownunicast, and Multicast (BUM) traffic and routing engine switchovers which are critical for network stability.

items.synopsis: Enhancement to retain route-target community after auto-import VRF routes
items.description: On all Junos OS and Junos OS Evolved platforms, an enhancement added to retain the route-target community after auto-importing Virtual Routing and Forwarding (VRF) routes from an Ethernet Virtual Private Network (EVPN) route to an IP Virtual Private Network (IPVPN) route.

items.synopsis: The FPC crashes when VLANs on an AE interface are updated or deleted
items.description: On all Junos OS Evolved PTX Series platforms with multiple VLANs on an Aggregate Ethernet (AE) interface and an Firewall filter with family ethernet switching and bandwidth policer attached to both the AE interface and its associated VLAN interfaces, a modification or deletion of the VLANs will lead to a FPC crash. All the traffic over the affected FPC will be dropped.

items.synopsis: The evo-aftmand process crashes when the prefix list is modified in scaled scenario
items.description: On all Junos OS Evolved PTX platforms, a filter installation failure under high prefix utilization leaves the system in an inconsistent internal state, and subsequent modification of prefix lists or prefixes in the in the same scaled filter can further result in evo-aftmand process to crash and traffic loss seen until process auto recover.

items.category: Enhanced Broadband Edge support for firewall
items.synopsis: FPC crash occurs after configuration changes are made to a service-filter on specific MX platforms
items.description: FPC crash and aftd-trio core-dump will be observed on MX platforms supporting MPC10E, MPC11E, LC9600 line cards, and MX304 after configuration changes were made to a service-filter which was in use by BBE subscribers.

items.synopsis: [Clocking Solution]:ACX7348: PTP performance is not working as expected for asymmetry config
items.description: This is day-1 issue of jnpr servo. It exist's on all ACX platforms where JNPR servo runs. Once the asymmetry configured at slave port, The error propagated to the down stream eventually cause this this perf issue of spike .

items.synopsis: PTP delay message sent from different LAG after RE switchover
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved ACX7332 and ACX7348 platforms, after Routing Engines( RE) switchover the Precision Time Protocol (PTP) delay message is sent from different REs when Link Aggregation Group (LAG) members are configured on different Flexible PIC Concentrators (FPCs) leading to PTP timing discrepancy.

items.synopsis: Interfaces Fail to Come Up After Repeated Activation and Deactivation of Ports with 1G SFP-T Optics on Junos OS Evolved Platforms
items.description: On all Junos OS Evolved platforms supporting 1G SFP-T optics , repeated deactivation and reactivation (~12+ cycles) of such interfaces can cause the interface to go down permanently. All the services and traffic running on that interface will be affected.

items.synopsis: CRC errors and packet loss are being observed at the peer device when using 1G fibre optic connections
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved ACX7509, ACX7348, ACX7332, and ACX7100-32C platforms with 1G fibre Optics, when the Inter-Packet Gap (IPG) setting intermittently falls below the IEEE minimum requirement of 8 bytes, and traffic passes through the PHY, certain receiving devices are sensitive to this reduced IPG, which leads to CRC (Cyclic Redundancy Check) errors and packet loss on the peer device connected to 1G fibre optics connection.

items.synopsis: On Junos devices supporting subscriber services acting as DHCPv6 relay randomly deletes IA_NA or IA_PD binding/route
items.description: On all Junos devices supporting subscriber services, in case of dual stack DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) subscribers with IA_NA (Identity Association for Non-temporary Address) and IA_PD (Identity Association for Prefix Delegation) bindings with lease times (For the assignment of IPv6 address to a client device), when a client initiates separate renew exchanges for the IA_NA and IA_PD, and once client and DHCP server are in sync with these timers, there can be a race condition at Junos device which is DHCPv6 relay, has not refreshed lease timer and can go out of sync. This can result in deleting IA_NA/IA_PD binding and route to get deleted for that subscriber only. This causes one of the leg for IA_PD or IA_NA to go down for that subscriber, which can result in traffic impact for that leg.

items.synopsis: Core and context for jdhcpd saved in /var/tmp/jdhcpd.core-tarball.0.tgz
items.description: When the jdhcpd process encounters an internal exception, the process may generate a core file and save the relevant diagnostic context in /var/tmp/jdhcpd.core-tarball.0.tgz. This data is intended to assist Juniper support in root-cause analysis. The impact is limited to the affected jdhcpd process instance and recovery follows the standard process restart behavior.

items.synopsis: Jdhcpd cores generated after upgrade
items.description: jdhcpd cores seen after upgrade with dhcpv6 for IANA/PD

items.synopsis: The hash collision for storm control profile indices will result in an l2ald process crash
items.description: On all Junos OS platforms and Junos OS Evolved platforms which supports storm control, when a different storm-control profile is applied for interface where these profile have same profile index allocated then the storm control profile configuration and system state will not be in sync and a different profile will be applied for interface binding due to profile index collision which results into l2ald process crash.

items.synopsis: A buffer overflow during IPv6 NDP operations in an EVPN environment caused segmentation faults leading to FPC crash files and repeated reboots
items.description: On JunOS MX240/MX480/MX960/MX2008/MX2010/MX2020 platforms with MPC10E/MPC11E line cards as well as the MX304 platform, an issue in IPv6 EVPN (Ethernet Virtual Private Network) during NDP (Neighbor Discovery Protocol) resolicitation of a link local target address causes the system to use the IRB link local address in outgoing packets. Stack corruption happens when handling the IRB link local address and resulting in continuous FPC (Flexible PIC Concentrator) reboots (around 3 or 4 times) and crash files generation.

items.synopsis: Retimer/gearbox ports on LC1202 line card might take long duration to bring an interface back up
items.description: On PTX10004/8/16 platforms with LC1202 line card, retimer/gearbox ports on LC1202 line card take longer duration(~1500 msec) to bring an interface back up after short LOS insertion from peer device. This breaks sub-second hold-time down feature. The code fix enabled 'fast linkup' feature of retimer/gearbox ports. It helped the link to come up faster. Ideally retimer/gearbox ports take 1.5 sec to come up, but with this feature, links come up in 1 sec.

items.synopsis: Frequent link-protection flaps are observed for container LSP's with no change in member LSP
items.description: This is a timing issue seen on all Junos and Junos OS Evolved platforms when the optimisation timer expires for a member LSP (Label-Switched Path) when normalisation is in progress for a container LSP, this generates an unrequired route update leading to the link protection route of the LSPs to flap. LSP flap will result in impact on the traffic.

items.synopsis: The rpd process crash is observed after a graceful restart in the RSVP-TE scenario
items.description: On Junos OS and Junos OS Evolved platforms with Graceful Restart and RSVP-TE (Resource Reservation Protocol - Traffic Engineering) configured, an rpd crash is observed, leading to traffic impact after a Graceful Restart if a PVC (Permanent Virtual Circuit) fails to allocate correctly during this recovery process, leaving it in an incomplete or unallocated state, and the system attempts to clean up or remove this unallocated PVC.

items.synopsis: Excessive transceiver configuration mismatch debug messages could be generated during periodic monitoring
items.description: When a transceiver configuration mismatch was detected, periodic monitoring generated repetitive debug messages that could flood picd logs. This issue has been fixed by suppressing redundant log generation while preserving mismatch detection and reporting.

items.synopsis: PIM neighbors timeout on backup RE due to inconsistent state with master
items.description: On all Junos and Junos Evolved platforms with dual Routing Engines (REs), Protocol Independent Multicast (PIM) neighborship is not be maintained on the backup Routing Engine after a ppmd-agent restart. This can lead to loss of PIM neighbor state on the backup RE.

items.synopsis: PFE Crash observed platforms where PKI and SSL-Proxy services are configured
items.description: In stressful conditions, FPC crash observed and core file generated when PKI (Public key infrastructure) and SSL-Proxy (Secure Sockets Layer) services are configured, on all Junos platforms supporting PKI and SSL-Proxy services (MX, PTX, SRX).

items.synopsis: PFE crash due to memory corruption when STP is enabled
items.description: On all Junos Platforms, a rare memory corruption condition may occur in the Packet Forwarding Engine (PFE) when Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) is enabled and operating in default (distributed) mode. When the issue is triggered, the PFE crashes and a dc-pfe core file is generated. The exact trigger for the memory corruption is currently unknown.

items.category: RPD route tables, resolver, routing instances, static routes
items.synopsis: The rpd process crashes in a vrf having EVPN-VXLAN routes with specific configuration.
items.description: In all Junos and Junos OS Evolved platforms, when EVPN-VXLAN (Ethernet Virtual Private Network-Virtual Extensible LAN) routes are present in a VRF (Virtual Routing and Forwarding), configuring a generate route in same vrf can cause rpd (Routing Protocol Daemon) to crash and restart. Generate route configuration has to be removed to recover from this behaviour.

items.synopsis: MPC restart during commit when modifying the prefix-list in firewall filters
items.description: On MX platforms with MPC7E-MRATE line cards, committing firewall filter changes that include prefix-list match conditions can cause an MPC (Modular Port Concentrator) restart.

items.category: UI Infrastructure - mgd, DAX API, DDL/ODL
items.synopsis: RPC crash when non-ASCII character is included in XML data result
GNMI Get on openconfig returns not-found when only root-level openconfig metadata is configured
items.description: On Junos Evolved platforms, a gNMI Get request for the OpenConfig root (origin: openconfig, type CONFIG) returns a NOT_FOUND error when only root-level OpenConfig metadata is configured and no OpenConfig configuration data nodes are present. In this scenario, the configured OpenConfig metadata is not returned unless at least one OpenConfig configuration subtree exists.

items.synopsis: BIOS version 22.01 - for ACX7024 - System crashes due to a CPU glitch
items.description: On Junos Evolved ACX7024 and ACX7024X platforms, the system crashes, and a kernel crash is generated due to a random CPU error.

items.synopsis: rpd crash on backup RE during switchover due to VPLS Auto-Site mismatch
items.description: An rpd core triggered on the backup Routing Engine after a switchover due to an assertion failure in within the context of L2VPN VPLS auto-site processing, caused by a mismatch between the auto-site claim-id/site-id and the local site-id associated with interfaces in the VPLS IFL repository for a given instance, leading to stale interface entries being referenced during auto-site processing.

items.synopsis: I2C alarm and traffic drop is seen with a type of QSFP on certain ACX platforms
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved ACX7100-32C, ACX7100-48L, ACX7100-32C-K and ACX7100-48L-K platforms when QSFP-100G-FR optics which has serial number starting with 2J4 is plugged in, it is observed that the port goes down with I2C(Inter-Integrated Circuit) access failure alarm and traffic is dropped.

items.synopsis: Routing approachs/protocols sees forwarding issue on Junos OS Evolved PTX10003 platforms
items.description: Routing protocols sees forwarding impact on Junos Evolved PTX10003 platforms when a nexthop transitions between forwardable and hold/reject states, causing the nexthop token to fail reacquisition and leading to unresolved forwarding plane dependencies.

items.category: Software build tools (packaging, makefiles, et. al.)
items.synopsis: NETCONF: RPC get & get-configuration display invalid json format response for an OpenConfig when adds a routing-options configuration
items.description: After adding a "routing-options" configuration via OpenConfig operation, subsequent "get" and "get-configuration" may display an invalid JSON format.

items.synopsis: gRPC connections fail when the gRPC server is configured in a VRF
items.description: On Junos and Junos OS Evolved platforms, when the gRPC (Google Remote Procedure Call) server is configured in a VRF (Virtual Routing and Forwarding) instance, , the connections through that VRF fail and the gRPC service does not work as expected.

items.synopsis: System connections are not established while Subscribing for OC path using ssl local-certificates after upgrading to 24.4R2-S3-EVO
items.description: System connections are not established while Subscribing for OC path using ssl local-certificates after upgrading to 24.4R2-S3-EVO. This issue is only applicable on 24.4R2-S3-EVO and 24.4R2-S4-EVO

items.synopsis: The rpd process crash triggered by LLGR stale timer expiry and late reconnection of unconfigured BGP peer on helper node
items.description: On all Junos OS and Junos OS Evolved, when Long-Lived Graceful Restart (LLGR) is configured and a Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) neighbor goes down and reconnects after the LLGR stale timer expires, the Routing Protocol Daemon (rpd) process crashes leading to service disruption.

items.synopsis: On the JunosEvolved PTX10003 platform, post-upgrade or reboot, alarms were raised before interface initialization causing false alarms
items.description: On the JunosEvolved PTX10003 platform, following an upgrade or reboot, alarms were triggered before ethernet interfaces became operational, resulting in false alarms on the device. There is no operational or functional impact.

items.category: EVO Layer-2 switching for BCM XGS Platforms
items.synopsis: Traffic from certain VLANs are not forwarded through the EVPN/VXLAN enabled spine switches
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved QFX QFX 5130, 5700, 5230, 5240 platforms, traffic from certain VLANs (Virtual Local Area Network) mapped to VNIs (VXLAN Network Identifier) on EVPN/VXLAN (Ethernet Virtual Private Network/Virtual Extensible Local Area Network) enabled spine switches are not L3 (Layer 3) routed, resulting in traffic drop.

items.category: PFE L2 forwarding features on BT based platforms
items.synopsis: IRB routed traffic is dropped when both hosts are learned on the same SP-style Layer 2 interface on EVO-PTX platforms
items.description: On all Junos OS Evolved PTX platforms, IRB (Integrated Routing and Bridging) routed traffic is dropped when both source and destination hosts are reachable through the same Service Provider (SP)-style Layer 2 IFL (Logical Interface) and associated IRB interface.

items.synopsis: Interface remains operationally down on MX platforms after transient flap during boot
items.description: On all platforms with MPC10, MPC11, LC4800, LC4802, LC9600 linecards and MX304, interfaces configured with hold timers remain in the operationally down state following an interface flap during system boot. When this issue occurs, Layer 2 and Layer 3 protocols on the affected interface remain down, routing adjacencies fail, and traffic forwarding through the affected link stops.

items.synopsis: jdhcpd.re.re0 cored at trace_file_close_internal (traceptr=0x7efc443b2bb0) at ../../src/junos_trace.c:188
items.description: When DHCP trace options are enabled, there is a possibility that jdhcpd could core. In general, traceoptions should be enabled only for debugging. They should be disabled once debuffing is done.

items.synopsis: Traffic blackholing (drop) is observed when output-traffic-control-profile is deactivated/activated on an ESI LAG interface in EVPN scenarios.
items.description: IRB (Integrated Routing and Bridging) next-hop is not updated with the latest QoS (Quality-of-service) attributes after output-traffic-control-profile is deactivated/activated on ESI (Ethernet Segment Identifier) LAG. This results in traffic blackholing after deactivating/activating the output-traffic-control-profile on an ESI LAG interface in EVPN scenarios.

items.synopsis: IPv6 frames are incorrectly padded
items.description: On all EVO ACX platforms ACX7100-32C/ACX7100-48L/ACX7024/ACX7509/ACX7348/ACX7908, IPv6 frames are incorrectly padded with 0's ethernet/vlan padding (trailer) while sending to the peer device. In our incidence, GTP transit frames with these added paddings are dropped by the sGW (Serving Gateway) which causes service disruption. 5G mobility signaling will be impacted due to this issue.

items.synopsis: FEC table reaches the limit with the error "Failed to program the hardware with an error - table is full" on ACX7K platforms
items.description: Due to FEC resource exhaustion, MPLS tunnel service programming fails on evo-pfemand on ACX7K platforms. New MPLS tunnels and some forwarding entries cannot be programmed into the ASIC. This may impact traffic and cause instability in MPLS forwarding, even if the reported route scale is low.

items.description: Telemetry subscription to path /qos/interfaces/interface/output/queues/queue/state/transmit-pkts showing incorrect result

items.synopsis: The rpdagent crashes due to the forward slash character being used in routing-instance name
items.description: On all Junos Evolved platforms, configuring a routing-instance name with special characters such as forward slash can trigger a 'rpdagent' crash causing traffic disruption.

items.category: Issues related to evo operations - libevo infra, typeinfo ..
items.synopsis: Objmon Memory Leak from Unreleased IndexReleaseConfirm Objects leads to distributord Out of memory and Router Reboot
items.description: On all Junos Evolved PTX platforms, long-term use of PFEtoken features triggers an objmon memory leak, where net:: juniper:: evlruntime:: indexrelease:: IndexReleaseConfirm objects are not properly released, causing distributord to be OOM (Out of Memory) and killed due to memory exhaustion.

items.description: EVO-Suite fails due to SSH reconnection timeout as textchannel creation to RE device fails after reboot

items.synopsis: PAA installation failure on reboot due to "Not found default vrf" error
items.description: When a device is rebooted with PAA installed in 25.2R1 , PAA installation on reboot may fail due to "Not found default vrf" error. This can be resolved by deactivating and activating or freshly installing the PAA configuration

items.synopsis: Management access via telnet disconnects under certain conditions
items.description: On All Junos Evolved platform, management access via telnet disconnects under certain conditions.

items.synopsis: .ssh/authorized_keys not synchronized when replacing a Routing Engine that contains pre-existing same-named local users
items.description: On Junos Evolved dual-RE platforms, when a replacement Routing Engine (RMA) or previously used RE is inserted and the new RE already contains local user accounts with the same usernames as users configured on the current master RE, the SSH files (.ssh/authorized_keys, .ssh/id_rsa, .ssh/id_rsa.pub) are not synchronized or merged. As a result, passwordless SSH login between Routing Engines fails, and commands such as 'request routing-engine login re1' prompt for a password, even though the system login user configuration is identical and fully synchronized on both REs.

items.synopsis: Rescue Configuration Check Fails
items.description: On all Junos OS Evolved ACX Series platforms, which do not verify the syntax and integrity of the saved rescue configuration file when performing a configuration check, rescue configuration check fails.

items.category: Port Mirroring feature on express PFE
items.synopsis: Network packets on the self-mirrored file shows the same timestamp on every packet with self-mirroring function enabled
items.description: On all Junos Evolved platforms, with On-device packet capture or self-mirroring function enabled, the copied packets into the PCAP (Packet Capture) file shows the same timestamps for every packet. This issue has no service impact.

items.synopsis: Intermittent "broadsync_lock_failure" alarms are seen on Junos OS Evolved ACX platforms
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved ACX platforms, "broadsync_lock_failure" alarms are seen intermittently without any external trigger. These alarms are seen as a result of internal firmware misconfiguration and affects PTP (Precision Time Protocol) functionality. The alarms are cleared after few seconds (~10 secs) once the broadsync lock is restored.

items.description: For 24.2R2-S4, If evo-pfemand crashed (using kill -6) when device same traffic scale configured similar this PR reporter configured. This will lead restart of RE new backup RE with "catastrophic error/hw misc" as reboot reason. For more details please check AT

items.synopsis: The ODL execution failure observed for cli 'get-interface-information'
items.description: On Junos and Junos OS Evolved platforms, the command 'get-interface-information' returns an error when called via RPC (Remote Procedure Call) and the XML (Extended Markup Language) response is validated against the YANG( (Yet Another Next Generation) model by the OpenDaylight (ODL) controller. There is no traffic impact because of this issue.

items.synopsis: The rpd process crash is seen during RE switchover
items.description: On Junos and Junos OS Evolved dual RE (Routing-Engine) platforms with LDP (Label Distribution Protocol) configuration, an rpd process crash in the new master RE is observed during a RE switchover.

items.synopsis: Crash in the rpd process after LDP P2MP LSP Identifier reaches its maximum value and rolls over, due to duplicate identifier allocation
items.description: On all Junos OS and Junos OS Evolved versions that support Label Distribution Protocol Point-to-Multipoint Label Switched Paths (LDP P2MP LSPs), the rpd process (routing protocol daemon) crashes when an LSP Identifier reaches its 24-bit maximum value (224 1 = 16, 777, 215) and rolls over to the starting value because a duplicate identifier is incorrectly allocated. This condition occurs only after prolonged tunnel flapping (typically more than 16 million flaps). When the rpd process crashes, routing convergence is briefly disrupted, and services relying on label-switched traffic are impacted until the process automatically restarts.

items.category: Issues related to Junos licensing infrastructure
items.synopsis: License process crashes when AE interface configuration changes on Junos OS Evolved platforms
items.description: A license process crash is observed on Junos OS Evolved platforms when Aggregated Ethernet (AE) interface configuration is deactivated and activated or modified.

items.synopsis: RSVP hello messages uses secondary address when primary/preferred address are present for same interface
items.description: On all Junos and Junos OS Evolved platforms where RSVP (Resource Reservation Protocol) configuration is present and a RSVP enabled interface has 2 IP address of which one is configured as primary/preferred in that case the RSVP Hello message uses the secondary IP address to form neighborship.

items.synopsis: Incorrect module temperature readings trigger unintended optics shutdown
items.description: On MX platforms with MPC11, LC9600, LC4800 Linecards, MX304 and all Junos OS Evolved platforms, optics modules intermittently reports extremely high false temperature values in "show interfaces diagnostics optics" command. This can trigger false high-temperature alarms, leading to unnecessary optics shutdown.

items.synopsis: Tactical Traffic Engineering does not work on aggregated-ethernet interfaces
items.description: On all Junos and Junos Evolved platforms, Segment Routing Tactical Traffic Engineering (TTE) does not work as expected for aggregated-ethernet interfaces. As a result, congestion is not alleviated or sent over TI-LFA paths.

items.synopsis: Command timeouts were observed while establishing NETCONF sessions over outbound https after configuring management-instance
items.description: On all Junos OS Evolved platforms, command timeouts are seen on the device while establishing NETCONF over outbound-https sessions. This issue is specific to the use case of NETCONF over outbound-https operations when the "system management-instance" configuration is enabled, the regular NETCONF over outbound-https operations (without "system management-instance" configuration) and regular NETCONF over SSH operations works fine. There is no control plane/data plane traffic impact due to this issue.

items.description: On all Junos OS Evolved platforms, PICD repeatedly created new SNMP trap objects without removing old ones, causing distributord memory leaks over time. This is tracked under TSB107540

items.synopsis: The FPC major errors seen after FPC restart on Junos Evolved PTX platforms and PFEs fail to come back online in scaled setup
items.description: On Junos Evolved PTX platforms, FPC (Flexible PIC Concentrator) major errors can be seen after FPC restart/offline or multiple concurrent PFE (Packet Forwarding Engine) restart/offline in a highly-scaled scenario that can result in the PFEs failing to come back online. This is due to offline timeout, FPC go into fault state causing services to impact. This is a rare case scenario.
